description: One piece of a file being uploaded across many tool calls, held as base64 exactly as it arrived. Rows live only as long as the Staged File Upload Session they point at. NOT a child table, and the reason is arithmetic: Frappe rewrites every child row of a document on save, so appending the six hundredth 200 KB piece to a child table would rewrite the other five hundred and ninety-nine. A separate table is written once per piece.

fields.description: The upload this piece belongs to.
fields.label: Session

fields.description: Where this piece goes in the finished file, counting from 0. Pieces may arrive in any order; this is what puts them back together.
fields.label: Chunk Index

fields.description: Decoded length of this piece, in bytes.
fields.label: Chunk Bytes

fields.description: SHA-256 of this piece's decoded bytes. Every piece gets one, so a corrupted upload can be narrowed to the call that carried it rather than reported as 'the file is wrong'.
fields.label: Chunk Sha256

fields.description: The piece itself, base64, stored exactly as it arrived. Long Text because a MariaDB LONGTEXT is the only column that holds 200 KB of it without truncating silently.
fields.label: Chunk Base64

name: Staged File Chunk
